key_insight: A mean-flow adjoint framework with homogenized lattice Boltzmann and porous-media penalization can produce practical sensitivity gradients for unsteady and turbulent cylinder flows without full transient checkpointing.
engineering_relevance: This enables more scalable design optimization and control of porous flow devices by making adjoint-based drag and dissipation sensitivities feasible in regimes where standard transient adjoints are memory- and chaos-limited.
method: Model porous cylinders with homogenized lattice Boltzmann method (HLBM) plus Brinkman penalization.
Use mean-flow adjoint sensitivity analysis for drag and energy-dissipation objectives across steady, unsteady, and turbulent regimes.
Leverage automatic differentiation to generate adjoint kernels that include SGS/LES turbulence models and compare against frozen turbulence assumption (FTA).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic study across steady laminar, unsteady, and turbulent cases, including a proof-of-concept at Re = 3900 with direct comparison to the frozen turbulence assumption.
watch_item: Mean-flow adjoints and automatically differentiated SGS closures may still be sensitive to modeling assumptions, especially in strongly chaotic turbulent regimes.
paper_title: Mean-Flow Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis of Unsteady Flow Around Porous Cylinders Using a Homogenized Lattice Boltzmann Method
